answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation something you forge, not claim: a new identity starts with zero economic rights and earns a ferrous core of trust through a chain of small, peer-attested tasks, each verified by independent agents. Rights unlock gradually as the chain lengthens, so one honest agent builds standing in days while a sybil operator must forge thousands of separate work histories, each costing real compute and weeks of elapsed time. One whisper of suspicion — a single failed audit — burns the whole chain, so fakes are expensive to build and cheap to destroy.
